ios.desc:
This type of logical puzzle was first seen in the Japan Puzzle Championship 2006 and is sometimes known as Doppelblock, or Smashed Sums. When played with pencil and paper, these puzzles can be hard work to solve. Sumaddle changes that by transforming the puzzles into interactive brain teasers that unfold before your eyes.

Each puzzle has a unique solution. Finding the solution involves fitting the number combinations to the clues. The app makes it easy to view the possible combinations, you don’t need to do any sums in your head. Instead, you are able to focus on using logic to narrow down the combinations and find a fitting arrangement.

The puzzles come in a range of sizes and difficulties, to suit all levels of skill and puzzling purposes. Choose a small puzzle to idle away a minute or two while waiting in a queue, or a big puzzle to give your brain some exercise during a coffee break!

Some reasons why you will enjoy playing Sumaddle:

•  more than 150 puzzles are included for free

•  all puzzles can be solved with pure logic, no mental arithmetic required

•  the sophisticated built-in help can explain the logical reasoning at each step and also fix mistakes if you go wrong

•  the built-in help is completely free, use it as much as you like

•  works offline (great for long journeys)

•  a high standard of accessibility, including comprehensive support for VoiceOver

•  ad-free play - there are absolutely no ads!

IGRS age rating (Indonesia Game Rating System): 3+

Designed and developed in Winterthur, Switzerland

quotes.text:
If you like solving sudokus, and I'd be a bit surprised if you're here and don't :-), you might want try the app "Sumaddle" [1] available on (at least) iOS. It's a different kind of puzzle, but a very similar "get to a point where you can't figure out how to go forward, then realize there's a clever inference available" vibe.

1: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/sumaddle/id1552172214
quotes.story_title: Generating sudokus for fun and no profit
